title: Pan latch survives the settings modal — stale pan_last fires a jump-sized Pan intent on modal close
detail: A pan armed before the modal opens is never closed: while panel_open the mapping drops moves/releases, so pan_last goes stale; after close, the poll's synthesized release fires one Pan carrying the whole accumulated cursor delta — a visible camera jump from a dead gesture.
recommended_fix: Close the latch on the surface-owning transition: in Toggle_Settings' open branch (or mouse_map's panel_open suppression branch) add `inp.panning = false`, mirroring the begin_draw/start_run clear-points.

title: Camera-fit derivation now exists in three copies; camera_fit's 'ONE source' comment is false
detail: camera_update, ~15 lines above the new helper, re-derives the fit inline instead of calling camera_fit — a third copy despite the 'ONE source' claim. The codebase's own convention (interp_alpha_from_accum 'ONE derivation', band_width 'ONE definition') treats this as drift-bait.
recommended_fix: Route camera_update's fit (and ideally view_compute's scale) through camera_fit so a future fit change (e.g. Dublin-board margins) lands in one place; fix the comment.

title: touch.odin header still documents Pan as 'a deliberate no-op in the executor today' — superseded by this diff
detail: The diff updated the stale no-op comments in types.odin and exec.odin but missed touch.odin's file header, which now contradicts the shipped behavior for the exact intent this job activates.
recommended_fix: Update touch.odin's header to state that Two_Finger_Pan routes to the on_pan effect (the camera now pans), matching the revised types.odin/exec.odin comments.
